title: "Get started"

## Installation

```sh
composer require phpstats/phiz
```

phiz supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 (composer.json allows `>=8.3 <8.6`). CI tests all three on Linux, and macOS is supported too. phiz needs only the `json` extension, which PHP includes by default, and has no required Composer dependencies. Examples that use the pipe operator `|>` need PHP 8.5, and each has a method-chain version for PHP 8.3 and 8.4.

| Optional | Adds | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vl-convert 1.9.0 (a standalone binary) | `svg()`, `png()`, `pdf()`, and image files from `save()` | [Installing vl-convert](rendering.qmd#installing-vl-convert) |
| Laravel (tested on 12) | the `<x-phiz>` Blade component and `@phizScripts`, discovered automatically | [Laravel and Livewire](laravel.qmd) |
| phit, or `phpstats/phit-polyfill` | predictions from formula fits | [Statistics](statistics.qmd#requirements) |

## A first chart

`Plot::of()` takes the data, `aes()` maps fields to visual channels, and a geom such as `point()` adds a layer. `Datasets` provides the classic datasets used in these pages.

{{< include _generated/start-point.md >}}

`$plot->save('chart.html')` writes a page that draws the chart in a browser. The page loads vega, vega-lite, and vega-embed from the jsDelivr CDN, so it needs a network connection. Image formats need vl-convert ([Save a chart to a file](examples/save.qmd)).

## Mappings and fixed properties

Mapping another field to `color` gives each class its own color and adds a legend. Fixed properties, such as a point size or an opacity, are geom arguments.

{{< include _generated/start-color.md >}}

## Layers

Each geom adds a layer, and layers inherit the plot's mappings.

{{< include _generated/start-layers.md >}}

Plots are immutable. Every method returns a new plot, so a base plot can be stored and extended in several directions.

```php
$mpg = Datasets::mpg();
$base = Plot::of($mpg)->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy');

$scatter = $base->point();
$smooth = $base->point(alpha: 0.3)->smooth(method: 'lm');
```

## Pipes

PHP 8.5's pipe operator composes ggplot2-style functions. `ggplot()` starts a plot, and each `geom_*()`, `scale_*()`, `labs()`, or `theme_*()` function returns a closure that takes a plot and returns the next one. The method chain builds the same specification on every supported PHP version.

{{< include _generated/start-pipe.md >}}

The functions and the methods take the same arguments. On PHP 8.3 and 8.4, `apply()` takes the functions instead of the pipe, and it also applies reusable fragments:

```php
$house = fn (Plot $plot) => $plot
    ->theme('minimal', baseSize: 12)
    ->size(480, 300);

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy')
    ->point()
    ->apply($house);
```

## Output

A plot compiles to a Vega-Lite specification when output is requested.

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `toArray()`, `toJson()` | the specification as a PHP array or JSON |
| `embed()` | an HTML fragment: the chart container and the script tags |
| `html()` | a complete HTML page |
| `svg()`, `png()`, `pdf()` | an image, through vl-convert |
| `save($path)` | a file whose extension picks the format |

[Rendering](rendering.qmd) covers each output, and [Laravel and Livewire](laravel.qmd) covers the Blade component.
